AWARDS & HONORS 
Jonathan Blake Waxler Prize for Social Justice 
The Jonathan Blake Waxler Memorial Prize for Social Justice was established in 1996 to recognize students who have 
exhibited a dedication to social activism, advocacy, community organizing, or civic engagement as a way of enhancing 
the dignity of all people. This year’s award winner was: 
Samantha Angelini '26,   Art + Design 
Samantha Angelini, an Integrated Studio Arts graduate, began 
volunteering at Arnie’s Thrift Shop, a free campus thrift store operated 
by the Office of Sustainability, and served as Thrift Shop Manager for 
two years. In this role, she worked closely with the New Bedford Women’s 
Shelter, My Brother’s Keeper, and used Facebook Marketplace to provide 
community members with surplus items not commonly used by college 
students, including baby clothes, household goods, and furniture. 
She expanded impact beyond the South Coast region by working with 
organizations to provide seasonal clothing to homeless veterans in 
the Worcester area, and provided clothing and personal care items to 
women in Tanzania. Through her mentorship of student employees and 
volunteers, she promoted sustainability, service, and community care. 
Newman Civic Fellow 
The Campus Compact Newman Civic Fellowship honors emerging leaders who are dedicated to social change and 
public service with year-long training, mentorship, and networking opportunities. The following student was selected 
as the Campus Compact Newman Civic Fellow to represent UMass Dartmouth for the 2026-2027 Academic Year: 
Komal Pandit '28,   Juris Doctorate 
Komal Pandit is a UMass Law student passionate about education, civic 
engagement, and public service. As the child of immigrants, she believes 
that understanding one's cultural roots is essential to fostering identity, 
confidence, and a strong sense of community. Guided in these values, 
she has served as a poll worker during the 2016 election, Vice President of 
Philanthropy for her undergraduate sorority, Delta Zeta, and an Alterna - 
tive Break Graduate Fellow at Suffolk University's Center for Community 
Engagement. Through UMass Law’s Asian Pacific American Law Students 
Association, she helped organize a panel on the impact of immigration 
enforcement on Asian communities. Komal strives to address the root 
causes of inequity by creating collaborative, informed spaces that 
empower communities and inspire meaningful, lasting change.
